variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'in the castle of the king's house' renders the construct chain the same way whether the qere carries the article (הַמֶּלֶךְ) or the ketiv omits it (מלך); English definiteness of 'the king's' does not expose the Hebrew article. The only note on the verse (Or, palace) is alternative_rendering, about the English for 'castle', and decides nothing here. Retain the qere base fallback.

Supplied 'and all': the Hebrew writes no waw and no כֹּל before אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, whose relative modifies דִּבְרֵי directly. Both words open the same coordinated colon and answer to no morpheme, so they are one added unit under rule 2, headed on 'all', exactly as the supplied 'and reigned' of 15.17/23/27. Competing reading: 'all that' on אֲשֶׁר as a supplied antecedent under rule 46's first rider — rejected because the relative has a written antecedent and the ASV's 'all' is a harmonization to the neighbouring formula.
Explicit pronoun takes only its own they (rule 20).
Participial predicate keeps its own word; the copula went to הֲ.

review_notes: ASV 'and all that he did' against Hebrew אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה: 'and all' is one added unit headed on 'all', matching the one-unit treatment of the supplied 'and reigned' in 15.17/23/27; 15.16's 'it' / 'and' remain two units because they belong to different clauses.

Competing reading for 'all that': supplied antecedent joined to אֲשֶׁר under rule 46's first rider — rejected because the relative has a written antecedent (דִּבְרֵי יוֹתָם) and the ASV's 'all' harmonizes to the neighbouring formula rather than building a noun phrase for a headless clause.
